newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clashes flare again in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Clashes flare again in Hebron.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinian youths raced from a funeral procession towards Israeli lines in the West Bank town of Hebron on Wednesday, hurling rocks at soldiers who responded with rubber bullets.
At least 10 Arabs were wounded, witnesses said.

The street battles flared a day after three Palestinians were killed by Israeli gunfire in the bloodiest violence in the town since peace moves came to a halt last month over Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Chanting their support for an assassinated Hamas bombmaker, an angry Arab crowd shouted "Yahya Ayyash, you are dead but we continue your path" as they accompanied the body of Nader Saeed, 25, one of Tuesday's dead.

Hundreds broke away from the procession and swept through Palestinian police lines to confront Israeli troops in what has become almost a daily ritual of resistance to the policies of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Smashing large stones into small ones on the pavement, youths threw the rocks towards Israeli soldiers in control of Jewish settlement enclaves that remain in the town under an interim peace deal.
Troops in full battle gear perched on rooftops and fired rubber-covered metal bullets.
Netanyahu, just back from talks in Washington with U.S. President Bill Clinton, insisted on Tuesday that peace could still be salvaged, while Palestinians called for action against settlers.
A Palestinian delegation planned to travel to Washington on Wednesday for talks with U.S. officials on launching an American initiative to save the Middle East peace process, a PLO official said.

"Abu Mazen and I will leave for Washington tonight upon invitation by the U.S. administration for consultation with U.S. officials on American efforts to launch an American initiative to save the peace process," PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.
Clinton on Tuesday said he believed there was a "fairly decent chance" of reviving peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians.
Palestinians had hoped Clinton would pressure Netanyahu to halt construction of 6,500 housing units for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, launched on March 18.
The building, which Palestinians say completes a ring of settlements around East Jerusalem aimed at pre-empting talks on the future of that half of the city, ignited a wave of protests.

"I believe there is a way to move forward," Netanyahu told foreign reporters on Tuesday without elaborating. He vowed on Monday to continue settling Jews in the Arab half of the city that Israel captured from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war.
Tuesday's violence raised to five the number of Palestinians killed by Israelis in nearly three weeks of unrest.
About 130,000 Jewish settlers, most of them armed by the Israeli military, live in heavily fortified enclaves in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
